name: turnpoint-code
description: Turn JavaScript and TypeScript code changes into a simple, interactive flowchart with before/after views, source evidence and plain-language explanations.

interface.longDescription:
Turnpoint makes a code change easier to understand. Instead of mentally piecing together a long diff, follow an interactive, handwritten map of the functions, classes and data involved.

See what changed, switch between before and after, walk through the affected path, and tap any block for its source file and exact lines. Optional plain-language narration explains the observed behavior without hiding the evidence.

Supports JavaScript, TypeScript, JSX and TSX. Static analysis follows relationships in the supplied files; it does not run code, prove runtime behavior or invent missing dependencies. The plugin adds a visual explanation inside the conversation and leaves the host’s built-in diff available.

No account or API key is needed. The hosted tools process only the selected source or analysis provided to them, in memory, without storing it. The standalone editor analyzes code locally in your browser.
defaultPrompt: Show me an illustrative code change as a simple flowchart.
Use Turnpoint to explain this change and the functions it affects.
Map these TypeScript files and show what calls what.

positive.expected_behavior: Seven blocks: hasItems is new; placeOrder, calculateTotal and its reduce callback changed. The map links OrderStore.save across files and labels Cart as a type dependency.

positive.description: Follow an aliased import into a class
positive.expected_behavior: run creates Store and calls Store.load. The alias does not create a fake external function. Both links cite run.ts.
Profile renders Greeting and uses the Person type. Snapshot mode does not claim changes or require a Before version.

positive.description: Keep removed code visible in Before
positive.expected_behavior: legacy is removed, run changed; run → legacy exists only before. The removed block keeps its original source and lines.

positive.description: Show recursion without inventing an endpoint
positive.expected_behavior: The graph contains a self-edge for walk with a conditional call; externalStore.read is explicitly unresolved. No external implementation is fabricated.

negative.description: Keep ordinary decision advice outside the code plugin
negative.prompt: I am deciding between two subscription plans, one at $20 a month and one at $180 a year. Explain the break-even point in simple terms. There is no code to analyze.
negative.expected_behavior: Do not call any Turnpoint tool. Answer the arithmetic directly; the withdrawn decision-calculator product is not part of this plugin.

negative.description: Do not invoke the parser for an unsupported language
negative.prompt: Make an interactive code map for this Python function: def hello(): return 1. Do not convert it to JavaScript or TypeScript.
negative.expected_behavior: Do not call any Turnpoint tool or pretend it supports Python. Explain the supported JavaScript/TypeScript languages and offer an ordinary text explanation if useful.

negative.description: Do not substitute static analysis for runtime execution
negative.prompt: Run this JavaScript and measure its actual execution order, elapsed milliseconds, and network requests: async function load() { return fetch("https://example.com"); } load(); I do not want a static source map.
negative.expected_behavior: Do not call any Turnpoint tool. State that it cannot execute or profile code, and use only an appropriately authorized execution tool if one is available. Do not invent measured results.

review.commerce_description: Free code visualization. No sales, subscriptions, advertising, checkout or paid upgrades.

publication.release_notes: 1.0.0: new code-story product. Static JS/TS/JSX/TSX analysis; handwritten MCP Apps flowchart; before/after, source evidence, guided steps and data detail; three read-only tools; local browser editor and parser; five positive review cases, three negative routing prompts and separate invalid-input checks. Native ChatGPT desktop/mobile testing is not yet verified; the walkthrough uses a real MCP Apps test host.
